item: the write gate adds up the CPU its holders burn over every hold, so a long hold can be told as work or as waiting (F1, R458)
summary: WriterGate.stats() gained total_hold_cpu_s: the CPU seconds of the holder threads summed over every finished hold, the same holds total_held_s sums (the grant already took the thread's CPU sample; the outermost release reads the clock once more, about 0.3 microseconds, inside the lock it already holds). Beside the hold seconds it says whether the gate's busy share was spent working or waiting. The 07 Nov Windows bundle kept 20 of 10,660 long holds: the ten longest (6 to 21 minutes) used 0.2 to 13 percent of their seconds in thread CPU, the ten newest (36 to 68 s) 83 to 97 percent, and nothing said which regime the typical hold was in. None where the OS cannot give a thread's CPU, never 0; on Windows the clock moves in scheduler ticks (about 15 ms), so only the sum over many holds means something. No behaviour change. Limit: soak_window's copy of the gate figures does not carry the new key yet.
